subject.title: Rebrand text-substitution filter on tool-call arguments silently misroutes file ops

question: Should plugin text transform output rewrites continue to touch executable/tool-bearing strings such as filesystem paths, or should OpenClaw define a path/tool-safe boundary for them?
rationale: The current behavior is public plugin/provider API surface, and the proposed path-aware fix changes compatibility semantics for both privacy-style transforms and rebrand/cosmetic transforms.

options.title: Define path/tool-safe transform boundary
options.body: Keep cosmetic prompt/display replacements but skip or explicitly gate replacements for executable filesystem paths and tool arguments, then document and test that boundary.

options.title: Preserve broad transform semantics
options.body: Treat all string-bearing tool arguments as valid transform targets and close this as accepted risk after documenting the operator hazard.

options.title: Require explicit plugin-owned policy
options.body: Move executable argument rewriting behind an explicit plugin hook or opt-in mode so each plugin owns whether its transforms may mutate tool inputs.

recommendation.title: Define path/tool-safe transform boundary
recommendation.body: Keep cosmetic prompt/display replacements but skip or explicitly gate replacements for executable filesystem paths and tool arguments, then document and test that boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the text-transform surface and is the strongest current-history owner for the provider/CLI transform boundary.
